newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise in sparse trade.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise in sparse trade.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Monday but dealers said that turnover was minimal due to a holiday in London,
"The market is strongly affected by the fact that London is closed. Generally, there is nothing happening," a dealer said.
At 1055 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.12 point from Friday's close, to 110.24 -- yielding 6.44 percent -- in turnover of only 650 million crowns.
Its June future inched up 0.04 point, to 109.88, with 93 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.23 point, to 88.20.
The crown traded at 3.8092 per mark, easing from its earlier 3.8080.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 67 basis points.
The Central Bank sold the five percent bond due 2005 and bought seven percent 1997 paper, but dealers were unable to say for how much. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
